title: Cutting a Nerve to Watch Repair and Pain
endLine: Controlled nerve injury isolates axon breakdown, regrowth, and altered pain circuits.

scenes.tts: Why can a cut limb nerve regrow when spinal axons mostly stall? And why can nerve injury turn light touch into lasting pain? To find out, labs cut or crush nerves and track what follows.
scenes.caption: Why can a cut limb nerve regrow when spinal axons mostly stall? And why can nerve injury turn light touch into lasting pain? To find out, labs cut or crush nerves and track what follows.
scenes.visual: Schematic horizontal view of one carried world: a paw on the left wired through a branched limb nerve and sensory cell body to the spinal cord on the right. A cut limb axon begins extending while a cut spinal axon halts; a gentle touch at the paw sends a red flash toward the spinal cord. Label 'schematic' in corner.
scenes.narration: Why can a cut limb nerve regrow when spinal axons mostly stall? And why can nerve injury turn light touch into lasting pain? To find out, labs cut or crush nerves and track what follows.

scenes.visual: Title 'Cutting a Nerve to Watch Repair and Pain' appears cleanly over the carried schematic paw-to-spinal-cord pathway while faint baseline pulses drift along intact axons.

scenes.tts: Cutting an axon, called axotomy, or a severe crush splits it in two. The proximal piece stays joined to the cell body; the distal piece separates. In mouse sciatic nerve, it looks normal for a day and a half to two days. After that latent phase, it breaks apart.
scenes.caption: Cutting an axon, called axotomy, or a severe crush splits it in two. The proximal piece stays joined to the cell body; the distal piece separates. In mouse sciatic nerve, it looks normal for a day and a half to two days. After that latent phase, it breaks apart.
scenes.visual: Zoom into one axon inside the peripheral nerve of the carried schematic world. A clean cut splits it into a proximal piece (attached to the surviving cell body) and a separated distal piece. A schematic time scrubber advances across a day and a half to two days ('latent phase') while the distal piece stays intact, then fragments into pieces.
scenes.narration: Cutting an axon, called axotomy, or a severe crush splits it in two. The proximal piece stays joined to the cell body; the distal piece separates. In mouse sciatic nerve, it looks normal for a day and a half to two days. After that latent phase, it breaks apart.

scenes.tts: In a peripheral nerve, debris clears over days to weeks, and the proximal tip may regrow. Human regrowth often runs around a millimetre a day. In the spinal cord, distal axons break down too, yet clearing is slower and incomplete. Many central axons stall. Is the fault in the neurons, or their surroundings? Controlled nerve injury separates breakdown, regrowth, and rewired pain.

scenes.visual: In the peripheral nerve of the carried schematic, debris particles fade out as the schematic time scrubber advances through days to weeks and weeks to months, and the proximal tip grows forward (labelled 'around a millimetre a day in humans', schematic). Pan right into the spinal cord: the distal piece breaks down too, debris lingers, and the proximal tip stalls.

scenes.tts: For lasting pain, labs use spared nerve injury. Two branches to a rat's paw are cut; one is spared. Calibrated von Frey filaments press up through wire mesh. Many labs take the force lifting the paw half the time as the withdrawal threshold. Days later, it drops: the rodent sign of allodynia, pain from normally gentle touch.

scenes.visual: Pan left in the carried schematic to a rat's hind paw resting on a wire-mesh floor, where the nerve splits into three branches. Two branches are cut while one remains intact ('spared'). Calibrated von Frey filaments of increasing stiffness press upward from below; a schematic threshold gauge drops over days as a thinner filament lifts the paw half the time.

scenes.tts: After injury, sensory neurons can fire with no stimulus. In one model, the spinal cord's sensory entry zone, the dorsal horn, loses inhibition. Then a light touch can fire a pain-signalling neuron. Pause and think: what can that paw lift not tell you?
scenes.caption: After injury, sensory neurons can fire with no stimulus. In one model, the spinal cord's sensory entry zone, the dorsal horn, loses inhibition. Then a light touch can fire a pain-signalling neuron. Pause and think: what can that paw lift not tell you?
scenes.visual: In the carried schematic, spontaneous sparks appear on the sensory axon, inhibitory brakes dim inside the spinal dorsal horn (labelled 'dorsal horn' and 'model'), and a light touch at the paw now fires a pain-signalling neuron and lifts the paw. The question 'What can that paw lift NOT tell you?' appears clearly above.
scenes.narration: After injury, sensory neurons can fire with no stimulus. In one model, the spinal cord's sensory entry zone, the dorsal horn, loses inhibition. Then a light touch can fire a pain-signalling neuron. Pause and think: what can that paw lift not tell you?

scenes.visual: Keep the question 'What can that paw lift NOT tell you?' on screen over the carried schematic; the filament gently presses and lifts the paw on a slow loop while a dim brain silhouette pulses gently in the upper right.

scenes.tts: A rat cannot say a touch hurts, so a paw lift is a stand-in. Separate brain circuits set unpleasantness, and spontaneous pain is hard to measure. Recovery over time may reflect which neurons survived, so labs trace injured neurons. Routes differ with sex and injury, and injury mechanisms may not act in disease.

scenes.visual: In the carried schematic, highlight the separate brain silhouette ('unpleasantness', schematic) apart from the spinal reflex, with a '?' by spontaneous firing. Shift to the sensory cell bodies: an unmarked injured cell vanishes while a neighbour stays, then a glowing reporter tag locks onto injured cells over time. Concise tags note sex, injury type, and disease limits.

scenes.tts: First, in 2020, Renthal and colleagues cut or crushed adult mouse nerves, then sequenced single nuclei from sensory ganglia. Injury suppressed the marker genes of neuron subtypes, and A T F three was required for full reprogramming.
scenes.caption: First, in 2020, Renthal and colleagues cut or crushed adult mouse nerves, then sequenced single nuclei from sensory ganglia. Injury suppressed the marker genes of neuron subtypes, and Atf3 was required for full reprogramming.
scenes.visual: In the carried schematic, highlight the sensory ganglion beside the cut peripheral nerve (labelled 'sensory ganglion (DRG)'). Its cell bodies carry coloured subtype dots; after the cut the dots dim as an 'Atf3' label lights up ('Renthal and colleagues, 2020').
scenes.narration: First, in 2020, Renthal and colleagues cut or crushed adult mouse nerves, then sequenced single nuclei from sensory ganglia. Injury suppressed the marker genes of neuron subtypes, and Atf3 was required for full reprogramming.

scenes.tts: Identity re-emerged on a time course associated with regrowth. An A T F three reporter's share held from one week to two months, arguing against selective death.
scenes.caption: Identity re-emerged on a time course associated with regrowth. An Atf3 reporter's share held from one week to two months, arguing against selective death.
scenes.visual: The coloured subtype dots re-emerge as the regrowing axon nears the paw ('associated with regrowth', schematic timing). Beside the ganglion, a steady bar shows the Atf3-reporter share unchanged from 'one week' to 'two months' ('against selective death').
scenes.narration: Identity re-emerged on a time course associated with regrowth. An Atf3 reporter's share held from one week to two months, arguing against selective death.

scenes.tts: In 2015, Peirs and colleagues deleted V G L U T three from mouse dorsal-horn neurons. Withdrawal thresholds rose after nerve injury, so stronger touch was needed. Also in 2015, Petitjean and colleagues removed spinal parvalbumin neurons in male mice. That caused mechanical allodynia, linked to lifting inhibition on P K C gamma interneurons.
scenes.caption: In 2015, Peirs and colleagues deleted VGLUT3 from mouse dorsal-horn neurons. Withdrawal thresholds rose after nerve injury, so stronger touch was needed. Also in 2015, Petitjean and colleagues removed spinal parvalbumin neurons in male mice. That caused mechanical allodynia, linked to lifting inhibition on PKC-gamma interneurons.
scenes.visual: Pan right into the spinal dorsal horn of the carried schematic. The 'VGLUT3' tag is removed from a dorsal-horn neuron (the neuron stays) and the paw's schematic withdrawal-threshold gauge rises ('Peirs and colleagues, 2015'). Next, a parvalbumin neuron disappears, lifting a brake icon off a PKC-gamma interneuron so touch triggers allodynia ('Petitjean and colleagues, 2015', male mice).
scenes.narration: In 2015, Peirs and colleagues deleted VGLUT3 from mouse dorsal-horn neurons. Withdrawal thresholds rose after nerve injury, so stronger touch was needed. scenes.tts: Activating parvalbumin neurons eased nerve-injury-associated hypersensitivity. Whether an axon regrows, stalls, or rewires touch into pain, a controlled break makes the mechanism testable.
scenes.caption: Activating parvalbumin neurons eased nerve-injury-associated hypersensitivity. Whether an axon regrows, stalls, or rewires touch into pain, a controlled break makes the mechanism testable.
scenes.visual: First, in the dorsal horn, the parvalbumin neuron lights up ('activated') and the paw's threshold gauge eases back up ('Petitjean and colleagues, 2015', male mice). Then zoom back out to the full carried schematic world: paw with filament on the left, regrowing peripheral axon and glowing traced sensory cell bodies in the middle, spinal cord dorsal horn on the right, all gently animated as one connected system.
scenes.narration: Activating parvalbumin neurons eased nerve-injury-associated hypersensitivity. Whether an axon regrows, stalls, or rewires touch into pain, a controlled break makes the mechanism testable.

scenes.visual: Clean silent end card displaying verbatim: 'Controlled nerve injury isolates axon breakdown, regrowth, and altered pain circuits.' over a softly fading schematic nerve line.
